newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S PROSECUTOR SLAMS GREEK LOTTERY DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S PROSECUTOR SLAMS GREEK LOTTERY DEAL.

text.p: Bulgaria's chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev told state radio on Wednesday that a contract sealed between the country's sports lottery operator and Greece's Intracom group was "shameful".
"First, I will ask to see the contract and afterwards I will seek a way to attack it," Tatarchev told Bulgarian state radio.
He added that after studying the contract he would estimate whether the law had been broken and whether Bulgaria's national interests had been hurt.

The Bulgarian lottery, called the totalisator, and Intracom said in a statement on Monday they had sealed a deal to introduce modern technology into the Bulgarian game, which would be financed by the Greek group.
The statement also said Intracom would not implement a decision of the International Arbitrage Court in Paris.
The Paris Court last year ruled that the Bulgarian lottery should pay Intracom a total 10 million including interest as compensation for cancelling an earlier contract.
A Bulgarian court said on Wednesday it would rule on the Paris court decision in a week.

Bulgaria's prominent coach in artistic gymnastics Neshka Robeva, who has launched a campaign against a new deal with the Greek group, met Tatarchev on Tuesday and told him the contract threatened the interests of Bulgarian sport.
Robeva told Bulgarian reporters that the Bulgarian lottery would lose 200 million if it sealed the new contract with Intracom. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
